SMTO-PRX-0017 — More than one VM matches the name you gave

GUID: 4886f609-14e6-4731-9a3f-d530db6115d5
Slug: proxmox-guest-ambiguous
Domain: PRX · Subsystem: prx

What happened

  • Your Proxmox server has more than one VM or container with that name, so SMTO stopped instead of guessing which one you meant. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to list the VMs on your Proxmox server, and find the ID number of the one you want. Every VM and container has its own ID number, even when names repeat.
  2. Ask for the action again using that ID number, for example "start VM 105". An ID number always points to exactly one VM.
  3. If you'd like to keep using names, rename the duplicate VMs in Proxmox so each name is different, including capital letters. SMTO treats names that differ only in capital letters as the same name when no exact match exists.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's reply names the single VM you meant and shows the result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't let SMTO pick one of the matching VMs for you.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Guest resolution found multiple QEMU/LXC entries in the current inventory with the requested name (exact match, or case-insensitive match when no exact match exists).

What this means

  • Guest selection finds multiple inventory candidates matching the supplied name/identity. Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.

Why this can happen

  • Guest selection finds multiple inventory candidates matching the supplied name/identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare current node, guest type and numeric identifier from inventory.

How to fix it

  • The error facts list the candidates with node, type and VMID. Pass the exact numeric VMID instead of the name, or rename guests in PVE so names are unique (including names that differ only in letter case).
  • List current inventory and choose the exact VM or container identity.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The selection resolves to exactly the intended guest.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
